reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output when the cited text creates no exposure — the rendered redline is byte-identical to the original paragraphs.

The cited paragraphs support the rationale: p0014 is a one-way invoicing/supporting-detail mechanic imposing obligations on Contractor, not an audit, inspection or records-examination right binding Customer; p0007's only access language runs in our favour (Contractor personnel must comply with Company security and system-access policies).

AUDIT is a protective cap on a counterparty right; the total absence of any audit right is strictly better for us than the preferred position, so flagging a deviation or 'missing' would over-flag against our own interest. Treating it as compliant rather than missing is the correct classification.

The failed deterministic check ('audit frequency limited') is explained and is heuristic noise here — no frequency cap can be located because there is no audit right to cap, not because audits are unlimited.

Rationale appropriately notes the residual watch item that a future Statement of Work could introduce a usage-verification or records-examination right, at which point the preferred limits should be applied.
